problem: The last column is labelled nNL/A (N·m). With n dimensionless (a ratio from a 1 kN unit load), N in newtons, L in metres and A in m², the product nNL/A has units N·m/m² = N/m, not N·m. Dividing by E (N/m²) must then give metres, which only works with N/m.
fix: Label the column nNL/A (N/m), i.e. N·m/m², so that (N/m) ÷ (N/m²) gives the deflection in metres.

problem: "Virtual work finds a deflection without integrating along the structure" overstates the case: for a truss the sum over members replaces the integral, but for a beam or frame the same principle becomes ∫mM/(EI) dx, an integral along the member. A student may think no integration is ever needed.
fix: Say: for a truss the work sum is a plain sum over members, with no integration along the members; for beams and frames the same principle becomes the integral ∫mM/(EI) dx.

problem: "The member's contribution is in the direction of the unit load" is loose: a single member's term is a scalar added into the sum, and it is the total Δ that has a direction. Also the answer skips the intermediate step that a compression–compression pair means both N and n carry the same sign.
fix: Both N and n are negative, so their product nNL is positive and the member's term adds positively to Δ, that is, it pushes the deflection in the direction of the unit load (here downward). The sign convention must be the same in both load cases.
